title: RESTest plan
description: A plan, handed to RESTest with --campaign and written in YAML or JSON: the strategies a run builds its requests with, each with its share of the run's time and the sources its values come from, and the operations the run may touch. 'restest run --print-campaign' prints the plan RESTest follows when given none. RESTest checks what no schema can: that the shares add up to 100, and so do the weights in each group; that a group chooses between at least two sources; that no two strategies share a name; that no name is only spaces; and that no list a plan names is called 'fuzzing'. It reports, without refusing the plan, a list named that nobody handed over and an operation under 'only' that the API does not have.

version.description: The version of this format, not of the file. Always 2.

strategies.description: The ways a request is built. Each request is built by one of them, drawn by share.

strategy.description: One way of building a request.

name.description: A label, printed in reports. Each strategy of a plan has its own.

share.description: The strategy's share of the run's time, out of 100. The shares of a plan add up to 100.

kind.description: What the strategy does. 'nominal': requests meant to work, built from its sources. 'fuzzing': requests that push at the API with values nobody sensible would send, from RESTest's own list of them first and from its sources where that list has nothing to send. 'mutation': a request the API accepted, sent again with one thing changed, falling back on its sources. 'sequences': requests meant to work, where a creation starts a short series of requests about the thing it created.

sources.description: Where values come from, asked in the order written; the first answer is taken. Each is written one of three ways: {source: <word>} for one of RESTest's own sources, {dictionary: <name>} for one dictionary by the name inside its file, or {weighted: {...}} for a group to choose between.

source.description: 'example': the sample values the document's author wrote down. 'random': a value invented to fit the shape. 'observed': what the API has sent back earlier in the run, and what it accepted in a request to another operation. 'dictionaries': every dictionary handed over with --dictionary, in the order handed over. 'default': the value the document says applies when nothing is sent. 'enum': the closed list of values the document says it accepts.

dictionary.description: The dictionary's name, as its file writes it under 'name'.

group.description: Sources to choose between: every one is asked, and one of the answers is drawn in proportion to the weights. Each source with its weight, a whole number from 1 to 100; the weights add up to 100, and a group has at least two sources. RESTest's own sources by their words, and dictionaries by name under 'dictionary'.

example.description: The weight of the sample values the document's author wrote down.

random.description: The weight of a value invented to fit the shape.

observed.description: The weight of what the API has sent back earlier in the run, and what it accepted in a request to another operation.

dictionaries.description: The weight of every dictionary handed over with --dictionary, as one source.

default.description: The weight of the value the document says applies when nothing is sent.

enum.description: The weight of the closed list of values the document says it accepts.

dictionary.description: Dictionaries handed over with --dictionary, each by the name inside its file, with its weight.

operations.description: Which operations the run may touch. Both members narrow, and an operation has to pass both. Left out, the run touches every operation it can test.

methods.description: Only operations with one of these HTTP methods.

items.description: An HTTP method, in capitals or in small letters.

only.description: Only these operations, each named by its operationId, such as 'getPetById', or by its method in capitals, one space and its path as the document writes it, such as 'GET /pets/{petId}'.
